title: Horizon Quantum Integrates Triple Alpha IDE with OQC's Toshiko Processor for Pulse-Level Control - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Horizon Quantum Computing and Oxford Quantum Circuits have integrated Horizon's Triple Alpha IDE with OQC's 32-qubit Toshiko processor at the pulse level, letting developers do pulse scheduling, characterization and gate calibration within one toolchain.

insights.claim: Horizon Quantum Computing (NASDAQ: HQ) and Oxford Quantum Circuits have connected Horizon's Triple Alpha IDE to OQC's 32-qubit Toshiko processor with pulse-level access to pulse scheduling, qubit characterization and automated gate calibration.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows software vendors moving down the stack into hardware control, a differentiation vector for publicly listed Horizon.
insights.locator: Quantum software developer Horizon Quantum Computing

insights.claim: Low-level pulse modulation and system characterization are typically isolated in specialized control-system software decoupled from application-layer development environments, and this integration removes the need to switch toolchains.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Unified toolchains lower friction for researchers tuning hardware.

insights.claim: Triple Alpha connects to Toshiko's control plane via a web API, allowing users to benchmark physical T1 and T2 and adjust pulse envelopes for single- and two-qubit operations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Remote web-API control access suits cloud-delivered hardware models.

insights.claim: Programmatic pulse access lets enterprise and academic researchers run custom dynamical decoupling sequences and optimize native gate fidelities on OQC's 3D coaxial Coaxmon architecture.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Opening low-level control may attract research users and make OQC hardware stickier.
insights.locator: For OQC, providing programmatic pulse access
